page_title: fob — Secure Enclave SSH keys, gated by Touch ID

sources.entry: fob - Menu bar SSH agent that keeps keys in the Secure Enclave and gates every use behind Touch ID. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/olivierzol/fob) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: fob
summary.one_liner: A macOS menu bar SSH agent that keeps SSH and git-signing keys in the Secure Enclave and requires Touch ID for each use.
keywords: sign git commits with secure enclave
use_cases: Protect SSH access to servers with Touch ID
Authenticate git push to GitHub with hardware-backed keys
Sign git commits so GitHub or GitLab shows Verified
Bind an SSH key to a single host to prevent misdirected use
Audit and check ~/.ssh for weak keys or risky config
Migrate an existing SSH host to a Secure Enclave key without lockout
summary.what_it_does: fob runs as a menu bar app and acts as an ssh-agent whose keys are generated inside the Secure Enclave and cannot be exported. Each fresh SSH or git signature requires Touch ID, Apple Watch, or the account password. Keys can be pinned to a specific host so they are refused for any other destination before a prompt appears. An optional reuse window lets one approval cover a few seconds of signatures, which remain pin-checked and audited. Decisions are appended to a SHA-256 hash-chained audit log that can be verified with a command, and a read-only checkup reports on ~/.ssh.
notable: Private key is generated in and never leaves the Secure Enclave
Keys pinned to a host are refused for any other destination before any Touch ID prompt
Tamper-evident SHA-256 hash-chained audit log of every decision
Open source under AGPL-3.0 with zero dependencies, installed via a single brew cask command
caveats: Tamper-evident audit log, not tamper-proof; the owner of the Mac is not protected against
Does not protect against code running as the logged-in user or a compromised remote host; agent-forwarding hijacks are a stated risk
